post.caption:
300 loaves before sunrise. Not one “Bismillah.” 🍞

4:40 a.m. Flour on your sleeves, the rent due Friday, and you count again — still short. Uncle Karim says “Bismillah” over every tray. Then the adhan from across the street: “Rizq is written. Fajr is now.”

“For indeed, with hardship [will be] ease.” (94:5)

This morning, before your first task: “Bismillah.” Ten seconds.

captions: 4:40 a.m. Flour on your sleeves. The rent is due Friday.
You knead faster. You count again. Still short.
Uncle Karim slides each tray in. “Bismillah.” Every single one.
Then the window turns blue. The adhan, from the minaret across the street.
He sets down the peel. “Rizq is written. Fajr is now.”
Your hands are still in the dough.
You wash the flour off your hands. Cold water. Slowly.
Two rak’ahs behind Uncle Karim. The ovens can wait.
Friday is still Friday. But you’re not carrying it alone anymore.

end.gold: This morning, before your first task: “Bismillah.” Ten seconds.
